text:
Leila: Quick heads up — we're rolling an RBAC tweak for onprem nodes tomorrow AM. Need alignment on service-account scoping + KMS proxy access and what we log for audit. Anybody oncall?
Jordan: I'm oncall. What's the specific scoping change?
Leila: Narrowing node-agent SA to only secrets:decrypt for the customer-keystore KMS key; removing broad editor perms from the deployment pipeline SA.
Sam: Do we have a list of services that currently rely on editor perms? I can run a drycheck.
Maria: I have a quick inventory: deploy-pipeline, metrics-shipper, vault-sync, and a legacy cert-rotator. The cert-rotator still uses wide perms.
Leila: We need cert-rotator migrated to a scoped role or to use the KMS-proxy sidecar. Prefer proxy for airgapped sites.
Jordan: Agreed. For proxy we need to ensure the proxy can only call KMS:Decrypt for specific keys. Also audit logs must show caller identity and key id.
Sam: On the logs side, ops wants to keep a copy in splunk for 90d. Is that realistic for private deployments?
ops-oncall: We can ship a compressed stream; retention is configurable per-customer. But we need to be explicit in runbook.
Leila: Adding runbook note: https://go/redwood/runbooks/onprem-kms (draft). Please review.
Maria: Two concerns: 1) netpols — if we lock down egress too aggressively the KMS proxy may fail to reach internal HSM endpoints; 2) onboarding customers with on-prem HSMs — key URIs differ.
Jordan: For netpols, let's allow DNS + proxy endpoint + metrics endpoint only from the agent namespace. Example netpol snippet:```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-agent-to-proxy
  namespace: redwood-agent
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      role: agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          component: kms-proxy
      podSelector: {}
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
Sam: Nice. Also, ensure netpols allow MTLS to the HSM IP range for on-prem installs.
Leila: On RBAC YAML — example RoleBinding to scope decrypt only:```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  namespace: redwood-agent
  name: agent-kms-decrypt
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  verbs: ["get"]
---
kind: RoleBinding
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: agent-kms-decrypt-binding
  namespace: redwood-agent
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: node-agent
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: agent-kms-decrypt
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```
Maria: That Role looks okay but secrets:get isn't directly KMS decrypt — make sure the workflow doesn't expect rewrite of existing code paths.
Sam: If we move decrypt path to proxy, node-agent only calls the proxy with the key-id header. Proxy authenticates with its own service account that has kms:Decrypt on the key.
ops-oncall: Can we add an audit annotation at proxy level with request_id and original_sa? That helps forensic.
Jordan: Yes — proxy will add x-original-sa and return it to logs. Also we should sign the proxy logs with a rolling key and ship to splunk.
Leila: Related vuln triage: vuln scanner flagged a CVE in an older proxy lib (CVE-2026-0001). We patched in the hosted images, but onprem customers might still be on the old image.
Maria: Risk: remote code execution in proxy if exploited. Action: push patched image and coordinate a kube rollout for onprem customers.
Sam: Can we do a canary rollout for a subset of onprem hosts? We have a label strategy: env=canary.
Leila: Yes: canary first, then 30% rolling, full. We'll add a feature flag to proxy to disable optional parsing that triggered the vuln.
Jordan: Also add an emergency rollback plan in case proxy fails: fallback to direct KMS calls from node-agent but with strict audit and rate limiting. Documented in runbook.
ops-oncall: I'll schedule the rollout window and send the notice to customers with onprem contracts.
Leila: One more: audit logging content. We must log: timestamp, original_sa, proxy_sa, key_id, action(decrypt/encrypt), request_id, src_ip, and whether HSM attestation passed. Keep logs immutable for 90d.
Maria: For immutability, we can write to an append-only S3 prefix (or local object store with signed receipts) depending on site.
Sam: I'll prototype a small shim that signs logs with a per-cluster ed25519 key and uploads.
Jordan: OK. Action items recap: 1) Sam — run inventory for services with editor perms and migrate cert-rotator (due EOD). 2) Maria — prepare patched proxy image and canary plan (due tomorrow AM). 3) Ops-oncall — schedule rollout window and customer notice (today). 4) Leila — update runbook audit sections and emergency rollback steps.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled patch image build started for redwood/kms-proxy:v2026.1 — build 873 in pipeline.
Leila: Thanks everyone. If anything blocks, ping in this thread. We'll also do a dry-run in staging cluster at 03:00 UTC.
